LESSON: THE BIRTH OF MOSES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Bible
Topic 2.7: The Birth of Moses

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on The Birth of Moses. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How was Moses protected by God?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what The Birth of Moses means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of The Birth of Moses from Kenya
3. practise The Birth of Moses in clear steps
4. apply The Birth of Moses in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: THE BIRTH OF MOSES
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
The Birth of Moses helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: THE BIRTH OF MOSES
Study The Birth of Moses like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what The Birth of Moses means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what The Birth of Moses means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what The Birth of Moses means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “The Birth of Moses” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what The Birth of Moses means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of The Birth of Moses from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of The Birth of Moses from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of The Birth of Moses from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Birth of Moses in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of The Birth of Moses from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise The Birth of Moses in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise The Birth of Moses in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise The Birth of Moses in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise The Birth of Moses in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply The Birth of Moses in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply The Birth of Moses in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply The Birth of Moses in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “The Birth of Moses” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply The Birth of Moses in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what The Birth of Moses is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “The Birth of Moses” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what The Birth of Moses means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Birth of Moses in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of The Birth of Moses from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise The Birth of Moses in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “The Birth of Moses” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply The Birth of Moses in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach The Birth of Moses to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what The Birth of Moses means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of The Birth of Moses from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise The Birth of Moses in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of The Birth of Moses from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for The Birth of Moses: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study The Birth of Moses?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How was Moses protected by God?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what The Birth of Moses means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what The Birth of Moses means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of The Birth of Moses from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
